pages.text: "Grandpa, I want to take big steps like you!" Nils the little bear stretched a foot toward a big footprint. With his short legs, his toes barely reached it. Huge footprints strode ahead.
Nils jumped toward the next footprint and plunged into the snow. Only his blue boots stuck out. "I am all right! I will make big footprints too."
Another jump, another slip. Nils kept falling in the snow. Snow got inside his blue boots, chilling his feet. Grandpa was already far ahead.
Nils sat in the snow and looked at his feet. Beside Grandpa's footprint, a foot was less than half its size. "Why are my feet so small?" His shoulders drooped.
Grandpa Bruno came back and sat beside him. "Nils, look back at the way we came." Nils turned his head.
Two lines of footprints crossed the snow. Grandpa's were big, with pointed toes. Nils's were small and square. "Those squares are my boot prints!" His eyes opened wide.
"The big prints are Grandpa's. And the little prints?" Grandpa asked. Nils grinned. "The little footprints are mine!"
Nils no longer stepped in Grandpa's footprints. Crunch, crunch, he walked in his own stride beside them. Square prints followed one another.

Nils raised both paws high above his head. "The little footprints are mine! One, walk in my own stride! Two, crunch along side by side! Three, look back!" Two lines of footprints stretched from the cabin to the shed.
Grandpa lifted Nils high and rubbed cheeks with him. Even if they differ from others, only you can make your footprints. "Let us walk side by side tomorrow too! The little footprints are mine!"
